functionality.rationale: A weak harness could make XT-032 accept UI simulations instead of real packaged discovery, pairing, transfer, cancellation, and cleanup.

security.rationale: The harness must prove authenticated identity and hostile-peer rejection without logging identity material or bypassing production boundaries.

performance.rationale: Process orchestration and artifacts must be bounded so cross-platform CI remains deterministic.

compatibility.rationale: The same packaged workflow and evidence contract must operate on macOS, Windows, and qualified Linux.

concurrency.rationale: Two child processes, event streams, timeouts, cancellation, and teardown can race and produce false passes or leaked processes.

platform.rationale: The vertical slice cannot be accepted until packaged sender and receiver roles are exercised across all supported desktop platforms.

persistence.rationale: The harness must verify exact committed bytes and prove failed or cancelled transfers leave no temporary or committed partial artifact.

adr.rationale: The task adds executable evidence for existing product and security contracts.

architecture.rationale: Only integration-test and CI infrastructure change.

roadmap.rationale: XT-032 alone accepts the evidence and updates the vertical-slice roadmap.
